prompt_text: I am planning a trip. Should I book on Airbnb, Vrbo, or Booking.com, and how do I find a good host?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer
- There’s no single “best” platform — pick the one that matches what you need:
  - Airbnb: widest selection (private rooms, whole homes, experiences), strong host profiles (Superhost, Airbnb Plus), good for flexible stays and unique properties.
  - Vrbo: focused on whole-home rentals and family groups; often better for larger properties, fewer shared-space listings.
  - Booking.com: strongest for hotel-like instant bookings, many vacation rentals too, often has pay-later/free-cancel options and broad inventory in cities where hotels dominate.

How to choose the platform for your trip
1. Pick by property type and group size
   - Want an entire house or cottage for family/vacation? Lean Vrbo or Airbnb (Vrbo often emphasizes whole homes).
   - Need a private room/hosted stay or local experiences? Airbnb.
   - Prefer hotel-style options, instant confirmation, or pay-at-arrival? Booking.com.

2. Pick by booking flexibility and payment style
   - Need free cancellation or pay-later options? Booking.com frequently has those.
   - Want monthly discounts/long-term stays? Airbnb often has better long-stay pricing and filtering.
   - Prefer a single up-front price? Compare total price (nightly + cleaning + service + taxes) across platforms — fees vary.

3. Pick by support/guarantees
   - Airbnb: transparent host profiles, Superhost badge, guest protections (AirCover).
   - Vrbo: good for family-focused whole-home listings; has its own guarantees.
   - Booking.com: often easier refunds through property rather than a host, and 24/7 customer service for hotels.

How to find a good host (step-by-step checklist)
1. Use the right filters
   - Entire place (if you want privacy), number of bedrooms, Wi‑Fi, self check‑in, free cancellation, pet policy, parking, workspace.
2. Read recent reviews (last 6–12 months)
   - Look for repeated praise about cleanliness, communication, accuracy, and check‑in process.
   - Pay most attention to recent reviews; one old bad review matters less.
3. Check host profile and listing details
   - Good signs: clear, high-quality photos; detailed description; clear house rules; amenities listed; verified ID; response rate/time; Superhost/Premier/Top Host badges.
   - Beware: listings with few/no reviews or vague descriptions — not always bad, but require more vetting.
4. Compare total cost
   - Don’t be fooled by low nightly rates — add cleaning fees, service fees, and local taxes to know the real total.
5. Look for responsiveness before booking
   - Send a short inquiry and note how quickly and helpfully they reply.
6. Check cancellation policy and deposit/security-hold terms
   - Make sure you’re comfortable with the host’s policy in case plans change.

Good host signals
- Many recent positive reviews praising communication and cleanliness.
- Fast, clear responses in messages.
- Clear check‑in instructions and accurate listing.
- Verified ID, Superhost/Top Host/Airbnb Plus or similar badge.
- Clear refund/cancellation and deposit policies.
- Professional presentation: good photos and a complete amenity list.

Red flags to avoid
- Host asks to pay or communicate off-platform.
- Inconsistent or poor-quality photos vs. description.
- Repeated reviews about cleanliness, safety, or rude host.
- Very strict cancellation with high cleaning or hidden extra fees.
- Host refuses to provide basic info (parking, access, exact check-in).

Questions to ask hosts before booking (short template)
- Is the address exact or can you confirm the neighborhood? Is the street safe and quiet at night?
- Where should we park? Is parking guaranteed/onsite?
- Is check‑in self‑checkin or will someone meet us? Can we get early check‑in/late check‑out if needed?
- Are linens/towels/soap provided? Is the kitchen fully equipped?
- Any building rules or noise restrictions we should know about?
- What’s your cancellation policy and is there a security deposit or credit‑card hold?
- Can you confirm fast Wi‑Fi speeds if we need to work remotely?

Message templates
- Pre-booking inquiry (concise):
  “Hi — my partner and I are visiting [city] from [dates]. We’ll arrive around [time]. Is the listing available for these dates? Is parking/fast Wi‑Fi included? Thanks!”
- After booking (confirm details):
  “Thanks — excited to stay. Quick questions: what’s the check‑in process and exact address? Any tips for arrival/parking? Do you have a contact number for day-of arrival?”

Safety and practical checks
- Never pay outside the platform; keep all communication and payments on the platform for protection.
- Verify safety amenities: smoke detectors, CO alarms, first aid kit.
- If you’re unfamiliar with the address, look it up on Google Maps/street view and check nearby transit/shops.
- Save screenshots of the listing, messages, and booking confirmation.
- If you have special accessibility or medical needs, confirm specifics in writing.

Final quick recommendations by traveler type
- Families/large groups who want a whole house: start with Vrbo, then compare Airbnb.
- Couples or unique/quirky stays: Airbnb.
- Business travel, hotels, last-minute or flexible cancellation: Booking.com.
- If unsure, compare the same property (sometimes the same unit is listed on multiple platforms) and pick the platform with the better total price and cancellation/flexibility that suits you.

If you tell me your destination, travel dates, group size, and must-have amenities, I can suggest which platform to search first and give example message text tailored to your situation.
